name: Ithaka
note: Arkeisios to Odysseus to Telemachos, and out to Latium

Arkeisios.note: Grandfather of Odysseus; the line is short and the Odyssey says so -- Zeus gave Arkeisios one son, and he one son, and he one son. Od. 16.117-120

people.Laertes: Father of Odysseus, who gave up the throne and went to work his own orchard in old clothes, and was still there when his son came home. Od. 24.205-360

Odysseus.name: Odysseus (Ulysses)
Odysseus.note: Of many turns: the man who thought of the horse, and then took ten years to sail home from a war that took ten years. Roman: ULYSSES, through Etruscan Uluxe, which is why the Latin is so unlike the Greek -- and it is the Latin form that gives Joyce his title. Gives odyssey, for any long wandering. Od. passim

Penelope.note: Who unwove at night what she wove by day for three years to put off a hundred suitors, and then set them the bow-test knowing only one man could string it. Gives penelopean, of work deliberately never finished. Od. 2.93-110, 19.136-156

Telemachos.name: Telemachos (Telemachus)
Telemachos.note: A baby when his father left and a grown man before he came back; the first four books of the Odyssey are him going to look for news, which is the oldest coming-of-age story in Europe. Od. 1-4, 22

Telegonos.note: Son of Odysseus by Kirke, who came looking for his father and killed him without knowing him, with a spear tipped in a stingray's spine -- the death 'from the sea' the prophecy meant. Hyg. Fab. 127; Telegony

people.Italos: Son of Telegonos and Penelope, who married after both their men were dead; ITALY is named from him. A tidy piece of Greek bookkeeping that hands the whole peninsula to Odysseus' descendants. Hyg. Fab. 127

Antikleia.note: Daughter of Autolykos and mother of Odysseus, who died of grief waiting for him; her shade is the first he meets in the underworld, and she tells him nothing has changed at home except everything. Od. 11.152-224

unions.note: Hesiod gives Kirke two sons by Odysseus, Agrios and Latinos, and the Telegony adds Telegonos. Hyginus instead marries her to Telemachos, which is drawn beside this as a cross-era bond. Theog. 1011-1016; Od. 10.487-495
By Penelope, his father's widow, whom he married after killing Odysseus without knowing him; that marriage is drawn beside this. Hyg. Fab. 127
Hyginus marries the son to his father's witch. The tree draws Hesiod's descent for Latinos and this bond beside it. Hyg. Fab. 127
His father's widow, married after he had killed Odysseus without knowing him. Hyg. Fab. 127
